output.brief: The complaints look like a brake-fluid problem, not driver technique or the pads. Northfield Motor Services refitted brake fluid during the bay closure from a bulk drum that had taken on water. Their warranty returns (LK-217, LK-224) measured boiling points of 152°C and 149°C against 255°C for sealed stock, and the technician linked this to soft pedals on long descents. Calder Road Garage fitted the same Tessaro pads but used sealed bottles, and had no warranty returns. The complaints are also concentrated on 11 specific vans, while drivers rotate across Upper Wend. I am fairly confident, but I have not yet confirmed that every complaint van went through Northfield. Next: this week, take Northfield-serviced vans out of service, boiling-point test and renew their fluid from sealed stock, and check the other Larkspur vans Northfield serviced before 10 September. Do not discipline drivers or retrain everyone. Keep Tessaro pads for now; the squeal link is unproven.
